pr.title: Count no threads on a pull request's row, even with its drawer open
pr.head: 75258cb835cecbba0d708eb388de022910d846be

summary: Projector's panel, the list above the Claude Code prompt, gives each pull request one row: its number, a state word such as threads or changes, its title, and then notes that name every other state that applies. Clicking a row opens its drawer, and while the drawer is open the row spells each hold out in full, such as checks failing for failing and changes requested for changes. A hold is one of the states that keeps a pull request from merging: a conflict, failing checks, a change request, or unresolved review threads.

Before this change, the spelled-out form of the threads hold was the thread count, such as 1 thread. So an open row put a count back on the row, and when threads was already the row's state word, the open row repeated it as a note. The drawer's file lines already count each file's threads, so the count said nothing new.

Now threads has no longer form. The row names it as the note threads only when another hold took the state word, with the drawer open or closed, and never counts it. checks failing and changes requested still spell themselves out in an open drawer. The drawer's file lines, such as + src/a.ts 2 threads, keep their counts.

groups.title: The row's notes stop counting threads
groups.kicker: How each hold becomes a note, and the test that pins it
intro: HOLDS lists the holds in the order the state word takes them. Each entry has a status, the short word, and an optional phrase, the spelled-out form an open drawer shows. notesOf turns the holds that apply into the row's notes, skipping the one that is already the state word unless the drawer is open and the hold has a phrase.

The change makes phrase a plain string, drops the threads entry's phrase, and adds isNoted: false to conflict. Before, a missing phrase was what kept conflict out of the notes. Now a missing phrase means the hold always shows its short word, so conflict needs its own flag.

checks.text: The row's state word and its color come from rowState, which reads only status and color, so they are unchanged. The review traced every reader of HOLDS, and threadCount now has only the drawer's file lines as its caller.

files.note: The panel's module. HOLDS loses the thread count, and notesOf spells a hold out only when it has a phrase.

checks.text: For failing and changes, open or closed, the notes give the same text as at the base. For threads, they give threads only when another hold is the state word. The review walked each case, and claude plugin test . passed.

conflict leads HOLDS, so whenever it holds it is the state word, and status !== shown already keeps it out of the notes. The review suggested dropping isNoted for that reason; the code is correct either way.

files.note: The open-drawer assertions now expect threads with no count, and no repeated word on a row whose state is threads.
